what_its_for: Becaplermin gel is used to help heal diabetic foot ulcers (open sores on the foot caused by diabetes). It works by using a protein that naturally occurs in your body to help new tissue grow and close the wound. It is meant to be used along with good wound care, not as a replacement for it.
how_to_take: Wash your hands thoroughly before and after applying this gel. Clean the wound as directed by your doctor or wound care nurse. Using a clean cotton swab, tongue depressor, or similar tool, apply a thin, even layer of the gel to the entire surface of the ulcer. Cover the wound with a saline-moistened gauze dressing. After about 12 hours, gently rinse the wound with saline or water to remove any remaining gel, then cover with a plain moistened gauze dressing (without more gel). Repeat this process each day. Never apply the gel directly from the tube to the wound, and never let the tip of the tube touch the wound or any surface.
dosing: Your doctor will calculate exactly how much gel to use based on the size of your wound. The amount needed may change as your wound heals and gets smaller. Apply the gel once daily for up to 20 weeks, or as directed by your doctor. Use only the amount prescribed — using too much does not help the wound heal faster.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, apply it as soon as you remember on that same day. If it is already the next day, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular once-daily schedule. Do not apply a double dose to make up for the one you missed. Keep a routine by applying it at the same time each day.
storage: Store becaplermin gel in the refrigerator between 36°F and 46°F (2°C to 8°C). Do not freeze it — freezing will ruin the medication. Keep the tube tightly closed when not in use. Do not use the gel past the expiration date printed on the tube. Keep this medication out of reach of children and pets. Do not leave it in a hot car or in direct sunlight.
what_to_avoid: Do not use this gel on wounds that are not diabetic foot ulcers unless specifically told to do so by your doctor. Do not use it on wounds that show signs of skin cancer or tumors. Avoid getting the gel in your eyes, nose, or mouth. Do not use other wound care products, ointments, or creams on the same area unless your doctor says it is okay. Do not smoke while using this medication, as smoking can reduce blood flow to the wound and slow healing.
when_to_call_doctor: Contact your doctor right away if you notice any of these: your wound is getting larger or deeper instead of healing, signs of infection such as increased redness, warmth, swelling, pus, or a bad smell coming from the wound, fever or chills, unusual skin changes or new growths near the wound, a rash or allergic reaction such as itching, hives, or swelling of the face or throat, any signs of cancer such as a new lump or unusual tissue growth near the wound site. Also call your doctor if the wound has not improved significantly after 10 weeks of treatment.
when_it_works: Becaplermin gel works gradually — it does not heal wounds overnight. You may start to see improvement within a few weeks, but full healing can take up to 20 weeks of consistent daily use. It is important to keep using the gel as directed and to attend all follow-up appointments so your doctor can measure your wound and adjust the dose as it heals.
special_populations: Pregnancy and breastfeeding: Tell your doctor if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding. The safety of this gel during pregnancy or breastfeeding has not been fully studied. Children: This gel is not approved for use in children under 16 years of age. Older adults: Older adults may use this medication, but should be closely monitored by their doctor. Kidney or liver disease: Tell your doctor about any kidney or liver problems, as this may affect how your body responds to treatment. Cancer history: Use with caution if you have a history of cancer near the wound site. This gel contains a growth factor that could potentially stimulate cancer cell growth, so your doctor needs to know your full medical history before prescribing it.
